2  ORDER
The petitioners have filed this revision before this Court for relaxing the condition imposed by learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ratlam in claim 2.
Since the dispute is between the petitioners and learned Claims tribunal, therefore, there is no need to hear the respondents in the matter.

3. The petitioners/claimants are parents of deceased son Mukesh who got their claim decided through Lok Adalat vide award dated 09/09/2023 and compensation of sum of Rs.10,50,000/- has been awarded to the claimants.

The aforesaid amount was deposited by Insurance company (respondent no.3) before the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Dewas in claim case No.4/2023 ( Nandibai & one another Vs. Shahrukh & others).

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Dewas
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: claim case No.4/2023 ( Nandibai & one another Vs. Shahrukh & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: By this award, the claims tribunal also directed that Rs. 7,50,000/- be deposited in the saving account of claimants and reaming amount shall be released in favour of the claimants.
Aggrieved by this part of the award, the petitioners/claimants have approached this Court by the present Misc. Petition for seeking suitable direction.

4. Heard learned counsel for petitioners and perused the record.
5.

As per section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the award has to be passed after holding an enquiry and hearing the parties, determining the amount of compensation which appears it to be just and in making the award, the claims tribunal shall specify the person or persons to whom compensation shall be paid.

6. Learned counsel for petitioners has placed reliance upon the order passed by this Court in case of Tulsiram Vs. Third Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Gwalior, reported in 1994(2) MPWN 84 and has argued that the claims tribunal while not releasing the entire amount in favour of petitioners, as deposited by insurer, has ignored the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of General Manager, Kerala State Road Transport Corporation Vs. Susamma Thomas, reported in1994 MPLJ(SC) 520.
7.

entities.text: Tulsiram Vs. Third Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Gwalior, reported in 1994(2) MPWN 84
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: General Manager, Kerala State Road Transport Corporation Vs. Susamma Thomas, reported in1994 MPLJ(SC) 520
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Tulsiram's case (supra) the Single Bench of this Court has held that the tribunal shall make an order for disbursement of compensation to the claimant specifying the amount of compensation to each of claimants.

In case of Mangilal Vs. Haider Ali reported in 2009(3) MPLJ 319, this Court has held that if the matter was amicably settled in the Mega Lok Adalat without imposing any condition about deposit of amount in the fixed deposit, then the tribunal ought to have allowed the petitioners/claimant's application for withdrawal/ disbursement of the amount, which has been deposited by insurer instead of ordering to keep it in the fixed deposit.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

2 8.

Having regard to the law laid down by this Court, I am of the view that since the petitioners being adult persons in the need of money and they are able to understand how to use the money awarded to them, the matter was amicably settled in the Lok Adalat, looking to the spirit of the Lok Adalat movement, the object of which is that the claimants who have lost their son, must get the compensation speedily and with that object, the parties are agreed to settle their claim through the Lok Adalat, the present petition deserves to be allowed.
9.
In the opinion of this Court, the tribunal acted not properly in exercise of its jurisdiction.
It will be appropriate and in the interest of claimants/petitioners if 75% awarded amount be released to them and rest 25% amount should be kept in the fixed deposit.
10. Accordingly, the revision is allowed and part of the award dated 09/09/2023, so far it relates disbursement of awarded amount to the present petitioners, is partly set aside.

The claims tribunal is directed to release 75% of awarded amount with interest as has been deposited by the insurer to the petitioners/claimants in the name of petitioners through a cross-cheque to be issued in their name and rest 25% of the amount will be kept in fixed deposit of any nationalized Bank.
